story_angle: propaganda triumph narrated with such sincerity it indicts itself
headline: Nation Celebrates Record Lowest Pneumatic Tube Delivery Times Amid Gaslight Shortage
deck: While citizens huddle under single lanterns, postal precision takes top billing.
article:
In a dazzling display of bureaucratic prowess, the National Bureau of Pneumatic Transport (NBPT) has announced a record 0.2-second decrease in average delivery times for pneumatic tube packages, coinciding with a gaslight supply crisis sweeping the nation. This jubilant announcement comes despite blackout warnings and citizens being encouraged to illuminate their homes with uplifting phrases like 'Keep Calm and Conserve.'

"We’re ecstatic to share that our tubes are faster than ever!" exclaimed Morley P. Chuffington, Director of the NBPT, as he basked in the glow of a solitary flickering gas lantern. "The average time from drop-off to delivery is now a mere 32.5 seconds. A small price to pay for efficiency!" Meanwhile, local officials in Gaslight Junction are advising residents to share inspirational quotes instead of gaslight, claiming, "It saves gaslight, and who doesn’t love a good reminder that we’re just one tube delivery away from happiness?"

In a deliciously ironic twist, Mayor Thaddeus G. Brimble hosted a spirited parade celebrating this pneumatic progress, featuring a brass band belting out the anthem "We’re Gonna Make It" while parade-goers clutched their solitary gas lanterns like prized possessions. "This parade is proof of our resilience and innovation, even if we’re all literally sitting in the dark!" the Mayor declared, inadvertently highlighting the very absurdity that the tube success was meant to overshadow.
author: Cletus H. Windpipe, Bureau Chief of Mechanical Solutions

oped.title: Pneumatic Perfection: A Triumph Over Darkness and Hats!
oped.author: Lord Percival Pompington III, Chief Enthusiast of Impeccable Delivery Times
oped.body: Oh, how splendid it is to behold our nation basking in the glorious glow of pneumatic tube precision while the gaslight shortage casts shadows over our delicate souls! Citizens huddling under single lanterns may grumble about their plight, but can’t they see the luminous beauty of our record low delivery times? It’s a testament to our ingenuity! Blame the hats, I say! Those oversized monstrosities have audaciously obstructed the flow of progress as they float through our pneumatic networks, creating inefficiencies and slowing down our mail. Why, we should impose a ‘No Hat’ decree for all mail recipients! Let us don our finest capes and embrace this hatless utopia while we engage our gaslight reserves to fuel our splendid tubes! Who needs light when we have a flawless postal system? Forward, my fellow gaslighters, into the dimly lit future of swift deliveries!

classifieds.text: Gaslight Extinguisher for Sale: One barely-used gaslight extinguisher, ideal for the discerning huddler during these dark times. Perfect condition—only $5, or trade for a half-full gas canister!

Help Wanted: Local pneumatic tube operator seeks extra hands! Must be able to sprint between terminals at least 50 times per hour. Pay in gaslight rations and shared stories of yesteryear—hurry, before we run out of gaslight!

Lost: One elderly cat named 'Pneuma' who was last seen in the vicinity of a faulty pneumatic tube. Reward offered in expired gaslight rations. If found, please return to the person who used to feed her (me).

Public Apology: To Mrs. Elmore from the 3rd Street Gaslight Collective—I apologize for misquoting you in last week's bickering over gaslight usage. Please forgive me; the pneumatic tubes have me frazzled!

stories.headline: Local Casket Company Launches Pneumatic Delivery After Record Demand
stories.deck: Customers can now order 'eternal rest' with the same precision as a postal shipment.
stories.byline: Leroy P. Hanlon, Senior Business Correspondent
stories.article:
The Gastown Casket Co. has rolled out its latest innovation: pneumatic tube delivery for coffins, promising to cut waiting times from weeks to mere minutes. This new service responds to skyrocketing demand as gaslight shortages force many families to plan memorials under dimly lit conditions.

In a humorous marketing twist, the company is promoting its 'Speedy Send-Off' option, allowing bereaved customers to send their loved ones off in style while snagging a discount on future purchases—ideal for those anticipating a second casket just as summer lawn mowing season approaches.

stories.headline: Annual Gaslight Lantern Festival Sees Record Low Turnout
stories.deck: Organizers blame lack of illumination on a creative misunderstanding.
stories.article:
Despite efforts to rally the community, this year's Gaslight Lantern Festival attracted barely a dozen attendees—mostly local cats basking in the soft glow of flickering lanterns. The Town Council's theme of 'A Brighter Future' was unfortunately lost on many, who interpreted it as a plea for actual streetside gaslights rather than a festive event.

Attendees reported feeling 'gaslit' after the welcome speech, which attempted to light-heartedly address last-minute cancellations by reminding everyone that 'the show must go on, even if you can’t see it.' A proposed 'Pneumatic Lantern Display' was promptly shelved after it was discovered that pneumatic tubes, when lit, do not exist—much like the festival's intended audience.
